final.memo:
We find ourselves in a period where the market offers little in the way of bargains that meet our standards for wonderful businesses at attractive prices. With the S&P 500 trading at roughly 28.45 times earnings, the yields available from equities are not only unappealing relative to their historical norms but are inferior to the returns available on risk-free government instruments [D04]. When we cannot find businesses that we understand, with durable moats and pricing power, at prices that offer a clear margin of safety, we prefer to wait [D01, D04].

Our current stance is one of patience. We have built a substantial cash and Treasury bill position, which serves as a necessary buffer for our insurance operations and as fuel for when Mr. Market eventually offers us more sensible entry points [D01, D08]. We do not forecast market directions, nor do we feel any institutional imperative to deploy capital simply because our cash balance has grown [D05, D06]. We will continue to hold our existing wonderful businesses and maintain our discipline, waiting for the day when the spread between equity earnings yields and bond yields turns in our favor [D01, D06].
